exposure: women with a history of recurrent miscarriage
women without a history of miscarriage
outcome: treatment with low-dose aspirin and/or subcutaneous heparin
cohort: 74 nulliparous pregnant women with a history of recurrent miscarriage compared to 4,176 nulliparous women without a history of miscarriage, all of whom delivered at ≥14 weeks' gestation from 2008 through 2013 at a Japanese perinatal center
finding: While women with a history of recurrent miscarriage had higher rates of advanced maternal age, in vitro fertilization use, and cesarean delivery, there were no significant differences in fetal/neonatal outcomes between the groups.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery rate was higher in women with a history of recurrent miscarriage.
